facts.claim: Cache tag invalidation lets you invalidate multiple related cached objects with a single request using simple text string tags: instead of tracking and specifying individual URL paths, you tag objects during caching and then invalidate all objects that share a tag at once. Path-based invalidation and tag invalidation both remain available and can be used together.

values.display: multiple related cached objects with a single request

qualifiers.condition: objects are tagged when they are cached

evidence.title: FAQs | What is Amazon Cloudfront CDN?
evidence.quote: Cache tag invalidation is a CloudFront capability that lets you invalidate multiple related cached objects with a single request using simple text string tags.
evidence.context:
#### Does CloudFront support gzip compression?
Yes, CloudFront can automatically compress your text or binary data. To use the feature, simply specify in your cache behavior settings that you would like CloudFront to compress objects automatically and ensure that your client adds Accept-Encoding: gzip in the request header (most modern web browsers do this by default). For more information on this feature, please see our developer guide.
#### What is cache tag invalidation?
Cache tag invalidation is a CloudFront capability that lets you invalidate multiple related cached objects with a single request using simple text string tags. Instead of tracking and specifying individual URL paths, you pre-tag objects during caching with descriptive labels (e.g., "homepage", "product:123", "user-ABC") and then invalidate all objects sharing a tag at once.
#### Why should I use cache tag invalidation?
Cache tag invalidation simplifies how you manage cached content. It eliminates the need for complex URL tracking systems or wide-reaching wildcard invalidations. With a single invalidation request, you can refresh all related content—even when those objects don't share a common URL path—reducing operational complexity and improving your cache hit ratio.
#### How does cache tag invalidation differ from path-based invalidation?

evidence.title: FAQs | What is Amazon Cloudfront CDN?
evidence.quote: Both methods remain available and can be used together.
evidence.context:
#### Why should I use cache tag invalidation?
Cache tag invalidation simplifies how you manage cached content. It eliminates the need for complex URL tracking systems or wide-reaching wildcard invalidations. With a single invalidation request, you can refresh all related content—even when those objects don't share a common URL path—reducing operational complexity and improving your cache hit ratio.
#### How does cache tag invalidation differ from path-based invalidation?
Path-based invalidation requires you to specify exact URL paths or wildcard patterns for the objects you want to invalidate. Cache tag invalidation lets you group objects by logical tags regardless of their URL structure. For example, you can tag all objects related to a product with "product:123" and invalidate them all at once, even if they live at different URL paths. Both methods remain available and can be used together.

facts.claim: Flat-rate plans do not need an annual commitment to get the best available rates. Plans are purchased for the current month's billing period and automatically renew until canceled; when you cancel a plan, flat-rate pricing continues through the end of the current billing cycle, and the distribution and its plan resources then switch to pay-as-you-go pricing at the start of the next billing cycle.

values.display: do not need an annual commitment

evidence.title: FAQs | What is Amazon Cloudfront CDN?
evidence.quote: Plans do not need an annual commitment to get the best available rates.
evidence.context:
The CloudFront Free Tier is different – it applies only to CloudFront usage under pay-as-you-go pricing. While it provides 1TB of data transfer and 10 million requests free each month across your account, any usage beyond these limits is billed at standard pay-as-you-go rates. Additionally, other services included in plans like WAF, DNS, and DDoS protection are billed separately based on their individual usage.
#### Is there a minimum commitment for plans?
Plans do not need an annual commitment to get the best available rates. Plans are purchased for the current month’s billing period and automatically renew until canceled. You can upgrade your plan at any time or schedule a downgrade or cancellation to take effect at the start of your next billing period. When you cancel a plan, you'll maintain your flat-rate pricing through the end of your current billing cycle. Your distribution and all associated plan resources will then switch to pay-as-you-go pricing at the start of the next billing cycle.
Plan signups and upgrades are billed at a prorated price and given a prorated usage allowance.
#### Can I use pricing plans for some distributions and pay-as-you-go for others?
headings: Is there a minimum commitment for plans?

evidence.quote: A multi-tenant distribution defines the base configuration that will be shared across domains.
evidence.context:
#### How do I get started with CloudFront SaaS Manager?
CloudFront is available as an option via the AWS console and APIs for customers who wish to manage shared settings across groups of domains. Here’s how to get started: 1/Define shared settings: Create a multi-tenant distribution which contains shared settings that will act as the template for groups of domains. 2/Create distribution tenants: Create distribution tenants that allow you to associate domains and their TLS certificate to a multi-tenant distribution. 3/Fine- tune control: Optionally, customize settings for distribution tenants by applying overrides.
#### What are Multi-Tenant Distributions?
A multi-tenant distribution defines the base configuration that will be shared across domains. It contains shared configuration settings such as origin configurations, cache behaviors, and security settings. Unlike a standard distribution, a multi-tenant distribution cannot serve traffic directly. It offers customizable, parametrized fields to meet each domain's unique needs. For example: domain-specific origin paths or origin domain names.
#### What are Distribution Tenants?
A Distribution Tenant represents a specific domain using a multi-tenant distribution. It inherits the base configuration from the multi-tenant distribution and must have at least one domain or subdomain with valid a TLS certificate.

change_items.title: Added support for sharing VPC origins across AWS accounts
change_items.summary: You can create a resource share and add VPC origins to it. This lets you keep your VPC origins and CloudFront distributions in separate AWS accounts, enabling your organization to maintain multi-account requirements. Other AWS accounts can associate the shared VPC origins for their CloudFront distributions.

facts.claim: When a CloudFront Security Savings Bundle term expires, standard service charges apply for your CloudFront and AWS WAF usage, and the savings bundle benefits stop. Before expiration you can opt in to renew the bundle automatically for another 1 year term.

values.display: automatically renew the CloudFront Security Savings Bundle for another 1 year term

qualifiers.condition: opt-in renewal must be chosen before the term expires

evidence.title: FAQs | What is Amazon Cloudfront CDN?
evidence.quote: Once your CloudFront Security Savings Bundle term expires, standard service charges will apply for your CloudFront and AWS WAF usage.
evidence.context:
#### What happens when my CloudFront Security Savings Bundle expires after the 1-year term?
Once your CloudFront Security Savings Bundle term expires, standard service charges will apply for your CloudFront and AWS WAF usage. The monthly Savings Bundle commit will no longer be billed and savings bundle benefits will no longer apply. Any time prior to expiration of your bundle term, you can choose to opt-in to automatically renew the CloudFront Security Savings Bundle for another 1 year term.
#### How does CloudFront Security Savings Bundle work with AWS Organizations/ Consolidated Billing?
headings: What happens when my CloudFront Security Savings Bundle expires after the 1-year term?

change_items.title: Amazon CloudFront Functions now supports logging to CloudFront access logs
change_items.summary: You can now write custom data directly into CloudFront access logs using a new helper method available from within CloudFront Functions. CloudFront Functions run lightweight JavaScript at the edge for tasks like URL rewrites, header manipulation, and request routing. Previously, you could only emit log data to Amazon CloudWatch Logs as a separate log file from your CloudFront access logs. ...

change_items.title: Amazon CloudFront Premium flat-rate plan now supports configurable usage allowances
change_items.summary: Previously, the Amazon CloudFront Premium flat-rate plan supported a single usage allowance, and customers who outgrew it needed to contact us to discuss custom pricing options.
